commits.summary: The default test run runs inline again, never as a verification job, and a passed run is recorded for the push and release gates
commits.body:
The user decided to take the default run out of the verification pipeline: as a job it overlapped other runs in one cargo target directory (VF-034), was cut off with its runner at the Bash tool's 10-minute limit, and skipped the one-at-a-time lock when queued from a line that predated it. verification/default_tests.py (queue, step, supersede, bisect, the unread-file list, flaky counts) and its tests are removed, with verification/default-tests-unread.txt and the watcher's default-tests event.

New lib/tools/default_run.py: a whole default run (test_costs.py run) that passes records the git tree it tested, as jj snapshots the working copy, and only when no file changed during the run, in ~/.cache/in-the-loop/default-runs.jsonl. The record covers a commit of the same tree, or one differing only in traces, decisions and job records. sync.py push and release.py cut ask default_run.py gate --run, which runs the default run inline when no record covers @-; --skip-tests stays the user's alone. Every test_costs.py run holds a lock in the workspace's cargo target directory, so two runs in one workspace take turns.

Docs follow: CLAUDE.md (Verification jobs exempts the default run; Tests says inline, the record and the gate; the tests: queued brief bullet is gone), runtime.md (merges run the default run inline, the watcher's default-tests row and the release gate), the prove-java-change skill, verification/README.md, lib/README.md, llm-dlc/README.md, brief-template.md (one inline test rule replaces the Inline/Queued policy, which also settles the mismatch left by the run-brief merge), validate_example.py's docstring, and a line in VF-034.

commits.summary: A proof by induction and a lemma's summary no longer stand in for a call that writes, throws, or reads what a caller can change
commits.body:
Three false proofs, each reproduced first on the checker as it was (lib/tests/fixtures/claims/claims/Effects.java, whose main prints what a JVM says): (1) prove --decreases on a method that counts its calls in a static field proved 'result == 1' where a JVM returns 2, because the induction hypothesis replaced the inner call and dropped its write; (2) with a throws clause, the hypothesis returned a value for an inner call the property itself says throws, and proved 'result == n' of a method that never returns; (3) a lemma about a getter, proved in the fresh state where its static field is 0, was used as a summary after the caller wrote the field, and proved 'result == 0' of a method that returns what it wrote. The same held through a callee, through an array a static field holds, for the default locale, and for a lemma whose own assertion reads a field.

Now: a method proved by induction is held to the write checks a summary's method already had (Options::own_induction says the proof is by induction alone, where reads are sound because the inner calls are made in the state of the call under proof); the hypothesis does not cover arguments on which a throws clause says the call throws (the induction then does not go through); a lemma's method, and the lemma's assumption and assertion, may read no static field that is not final, no non-final field or cell of an object that was there before the call, and not the default locale (Engine::reads); a summary is not used while its method's class is still being initialized. A lemma about a method of no parameters now compiles (its assertion is over the result alone).

Which existing results rest on these mechanisms: none uses prove --decreases directly; examples 286 and 288 use lemmas about PatternMatchUtils.simpleMatch(String,String), whose bytecode in the pinned 5.3.19 JAR reads no field and no array (javap), so their results did not rest on the hole; that the tightened checks still prove those lemmas is for a job to confirm. Verified by lib/tests/claims.rs (18 passed, among them the three new tests and the changed lemma test: a method that counts with calls++ is now refused at its read, one that only writes at its write), the summary unit tests, and test_costs.py run --changed (8 of 8 passed: cargo test's 33 binaries and three Python files).

commits.summary: A test run keeps what its tests leave in a temporary folder of its own, and removes it
commits.body: On 2026-11-17 no command could start on the machine: /tmp, a 52 GB volume held in memory with 1,048,576 inodes, had none left. 640,000 of them were in 18,000 folders named jvmcontract-equivalence-PID-..., which a check run without a work folder makes in the temporary directory and keeps for whoever reads its outcome; a test that runs such a check has no reader, and every test run since the machine started had left its folders there. test_costs.py run now gives each run a folder under lib/target/test-tmp as TMPDIR for all its commands (Rust and Python tests alike), removes it when the run ends, and removes one a killed run left. What is already in /tmp is for the user to clear: it is not this change's to delete.

commits.summary: Take the test run's own temporary folder back out: the user settled VF-036 with nothing to change now
commits.body: The change before this one gave test_costs.py run a TMPDIR of its own. While it was being written, the watcher of the rehearsals recorded the same problem as VF-036 and the user decided it: they raised /tmp's inode limit to 8,388,608, cleared it by hand, and nothing changes for now; who takes it up, and when, is theirs to say. So the folder is removed again here. It had also made two tests fail (test_claude_setup.py and test_performance.py look in the folders above a temporary project for CLAUDE.md, and found the checkout's when the folder was under lib/target), which a later attempt would avoid by putting it in the user's cache. The change stays in the history (vqntqptvslos) for whoever takes VF-036 up.
